column3: The Hebrew says “I may be built up through her”; BSB explains this as building a family.
“He went in to Hagar” and “her mistress became slight in her eyes” preserve the Hebrew images.
The Hebrew has “in your bosom” where BSB has “into your arms.”
The Hebrew says “do to her what is good in your eyes” where BSB has “do whatever you want.”
“Under her hands” is rendered as “to her authority.”
The Hebrew says the LORD heard her “affliction”; BSB adds “cry of.”
The Hebrew says “before the face of all his brothers” where BSB has “in hostility toward all his brothers.”
The Hebrew frames her second statement as a question and includes “after” the one seeing her.
